welcome: The Central Sierra Foothills chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America brings together people across our region who believe ordinary people deserve a real voice in our economy, our communities, and our democracy.
Whether you're brand new to organizing or have years of experience, you belong here.
region: Because the region is so big, we depend on shared leadership and on members taking part where they live.
goal: Build people-powered movements that make life better in our communities, while working toward a more democratic and equal society.

democraticSocialism.intro: New to socialism? You're in good company. Many of our members started right where you are, and we're all learning together. At its core, democratic socialism is a simple idea: everyday people deserve real power over the systems that shape their lives.
points: Democracy shouldn't stop at the ballot box. It should reach into our workplaces and our economy too.
Working people deserve a real say in the decisions that affect their jobs, communities, and futures.
Healthcare, housing, education, and dignity are basic human needs, not privileges for people who can afford them.
democraticSocialism.outro: This isn't about having all the answers. It's about building something better, together. You don't need to know everything right away. Learning happens by taking part.

membership.title: Join DSA and pay dues
membership.body: Membership runs through DSA National. Dues are what make you a voting member, because DSA is run by its members. There are monthly and yearly options, and reduced rates if money is tight.

membership.title: Stay active, at your own level
membership.body: Come to meetings when you can, take part in organizing, and keep in touch with the people you work with. Showing up now and then is better than burning out.

membership.title: Pitch in on shared work
membership.body: DSA has no paid staff here. Everything the chapter does, from tabling to campaigns, happens because members volunteer. We succeed when everyone helps a little.

structure.branches: Branches are local groups organized around a town or area. Each one runs its own meetings and local work, and its chair sits on the chapter's steering committee.
structure.workingGroups: Working groups take on one kind of work for the whole chapter, across county lines. Some run all year. Others form for a single campaign or action and wrap up when it's done.
structure.steering: The steering committee is the chapter's five elected officers plus the chair of each branch. It carries out what members decide and answers to the membership.
structure.encourage: You're encouraged, but not required, to join at least one working group that fits your interests and your schedule.

intro: Jobs, families, and everyday life are real, and most of us are juggling the same things. This isn't a list of requirements. It's what taking part looks like when you have room for it.
What makes it work is open communication. The more we know about your time and energy, the better we can match you with work that feels worthwhile and doesn't wear you out.
hopes: Come to general meetings when your schedule allows.
Give a heads-up when you can't make something you signed up for.
Help with at least one organizing effort.
Share the work, so no one person carries too much of it.
participation.fromUs: Support as you grow politically, clear ways to get involved, and respect for your time. We're not just building an organization that holds meetings. We're building a community.

standards.intro: We come from different backgrounds and political views, and that makes us stronger. We won't always agree, and that's okay. What matters is how we treat each other while we work toward shared goals.
communication: Be kind, respectful, and mindful of other people's time.
Listen, and leave room for others to speak. Before you jump in, ask yourself "Why am I talking?"
harassment: Harassment and discrimination are not tolerated. That includes targeting anyone for their race or ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, religion or non-religion, age, immigration status, economic background, or any other part of who they are.
This applies everywhere we organize: meetings, Slack, email, social media, events, actions, and one-on-one conversations.
standards.conflict: Conflict happens in any group. Our aim is resolution, learning, and repair, not punishment.

steps.title: Talk it through
steps.body: If it feels safe, start by talking with the person directly and respectfully. Many problems are misunderstandings.

steps.title: Ask for help
steps.body: If talking directly isn't comfortable or doesn't work, reach out to your branch chair or email the chapter at

steps.title: Work toward repair
steps.body: Leadership will listen to everyone involved and can help with a facilitated conversation. Concerns are handled fairly and kept as private as possible.

standards.closing: Solidarity begins with how we treat one another.

workbook.intro: This part is optional, but we hope you'll try it. Work through it at your own pace. There are no right or wrong answers. It helps you connect the ideas of democratic socialism to your own town, and start thinking like an organizer.
